# uup_monitor (Resource)

A Monitor: an `http` URL, a `tcp` port, a `ping` host, or a `heartbeat` your own job calls.

A `ping` Monitor, and an `http` one with `assertions`, are tested once from one location before they are saved (a Validation run). The provider runs it for you and waits for its answer.

The type and the target (`url`, `host`, `port`) never change: changing one makes a new Monitor.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "uup_project" "main" {
  name = "My project"
}

# An HTTP Monitor checked from two locations, with an assertion on the body.
resource "uup_monitor" "api" {
  project_id   = data.uup_project.main.id
  type         = "http"
  name         = "API health"
  url          = "https://api.example.com/health"
  interval_sec = 60
  locations    = ["de", "us"]

  headers         = { "X-Health-Key" = var.health_key }
  expected_status = ["200"]

  assertions = [
    { kind = "json", op = "eq", path = "$.status", value = "ok" },
  ]

  performance_threshold_ms = 1500
}

# A TCP port.
resource "uup_monitor" "database" {
  project_id     = data.uup_project.main.id
  type           = "tcp"
  name           = "Database"
  host           = "db.example.com"
  port           = 5432
  interval_sec   = 60
  location_count = 3
}

# A host that answers ping.
resource "uup_monitor" "router" {
  project_id   = data.uup_project.main.id
  type         = "ping"
  name         = "Office router"
  host         = "203.0.113.10"
  interval_sec = 120
}

# A Heartbeat your nightly job calls when it succeeds.
resource "uup_monitor" "backup" {
  project_id = data.uup_project.main.id
  type       = "heartbeat"
  name       = "Nightly backup"
  cron       = "0 3 * * *"
  grace_sec  = 900
}

output "backup_heartbeat_url" {
  value     = uup_monitor.backup.heartbeat_url
  sensitive = true
}

variable "health_key" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The Monitor's name.
- `project_id` (String) The Project the Monitor belongs to, `prj_…`.
- `type` (String) `http`, `tcp`, `ping` or `heartbeat`.

### Optional

- `assertions` (Attributes List) `http` only: what the answer's body must hold, up to 10. A Monitor with assertions is tested once before it is saved. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--assertions))
- `basic_auth_password` (String, Sensitive) `http` only: the password for HTTP Basic auth. Never shown again, like `headers`.
- `basic_auth_username` (String, Sensitive) `http` only: the user name for HTTP Basic auth. Never shown again, like `headers`.
- `bearer_token` (String, Sensitive) `http` only: a token sent as `Authorization: Bearer`. Never shown again, like `headers`.
- `body` (String, Sensitive) `http` only: the request body. Never shown again, like `headers`.
- `certificate_check_enabled` (Boolean) `http` only: whether the TLS certificate's expiry is checked. Only an `https` URL has one. Defaults to on where it applies.
- `cron` (String) `heartbeat` only: your job's schedule, as a cron expression in the Project's timezone. Set this or `expected_interval_sec`.
- `description` (String) A note on the Monitor.
- `domain_check_enabled` (Boolean) `http` only: whether the domain's registration expiry is checked. Defaults to on where it applies.
- `expected_interval_sec` (Number) `heartbeat` only: how often your job calls, in seconds (60 to 2678400). Set this or `cron`.
- `expected_status` (List of String) `http` only: the status codes that count as up, such as `200` or `2xx`. Defaults to `["2xx"]`.
- `follow_redirects` (Boolean) `http` only: whether redirects are followed. Defaults to `true`.
- `grace_sec` (Number) `heartbeat` only: how late a call may be, in seconds, before it counts as missed (at least 60).
- `headers` (Map of String, Sensitive) `http` only: headers to send, by name. You Up? never shows their values again, so after an import they read as empty until the next apply.
- `host` (String) `tcp` and `ping`: the host name or address to check.
- `interval_sec` (Number) `http`, `tcp` and `ping`: seconds between checks. Your Plan sets the floor.
- `location_count` (Number) `http`, `tcp` and `ping`: how many locations check it, which You Up? chooses. Set this or `locations`, not both; with neither, the Project's default count. Read when the Monitor is made: changing it later makes a new Monitor.
- `locations` (Set of String) `http`, `tcp` and `ping`: the locations that check it, by `id` from the `uup_locations` data source. Leave it out to let You Up? choose them.
- `max_packet_loss_pct` (Number) `ping` only: the packet loss, in percent, above which the host counts as down (0 to 99).
- `method` (String) `http` only: `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE`. Defaults to `GET`.
- `on_status_page` (Boolean) Whether the Monitor has a row on the Project's Status page.
- `packet_count` (Number) `ping` only: packets sent each check, 1 to 10.
- `paused` (Boolean) Whether the Monitor is paused. A paused Monitor is not checked and sends nothing.
- `performance_check_enabled` (Boolean) `http`, `tcp` and `ping`: whether the performance Check warns when answers are slow. Defaults to `true`.
- `performance_threshold_ms` (Number) `http`, `tcp` and `ping`: the answer time, in milliseconds, above which the performance Check warns (50 to 30000).
- `port` (Number) `tcp` only: the port to connect to.
- `rule_ids` (Set of String) The Notification rules that hear about this Monitor, `rul_…`. A new Monitor gets the Project's Default rule when this is left out. An empty set assigns none.
- `timeout_ms` (Number) `http`, `tcp` and `ping`: how long to wait for an answer, in milliseconds (1000 to 30000).
- `url` (String) `http` only: the URL to check.

### Read-Only

- `heartbeat_url` (String, Sensitive) `heartbeat` only: the URL your job calls when it succeeds. Anyone holding it can send a Heartbeat.
- `id` (String) The Monitor's identifier, `mon_…`.

<a id="nestedatt--assertions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `assertions`

Required:

- `kind` (String) `keyword` looks for text in the body; `json` reads a value at `path`.
- `op` (String) For `keyword`: `contains` or `not_contains`. For `json`: `eq`, `ne`, `lt`, `lte`, `gt`, `gte`, `contains`, `exists` or `not_exists`.

Optional:

- `path` (String) For `json`: where the value is, such as `$.status`.
- `value` (String) The text to look for, or the value to compare with. Leave it out for `exists` and `not_exists`.
- `value_type` (String) For `json`: how `value` is read: `string` (the default), `number`, `boolean` or `null`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A Monitor is imported as <project_id>/<monitor_id>.
terraform import uup_monitor.api prj_abc123/mon_def456
```
